title: Pruning, Mystical Seeing, the Two Essences, and the Final Cherubim
description: The closing teachings. T101 distinguishes withdrawals of evil that are painless from those that are felt — surface outgrowths (hair-like, sprouting again from the food taken in) prune painlessly; structural members of the natural mind, when cut, pain immediately. The teaching is a doctrine of discrimination concerning regeneration: not every laying-off is the same kind, and the soul must not mistake the trimming of surface for the cutting of a member. T102 (fragmentary) describes mystical seeing during sickness when the soul is briefly loosed — the loosening accommodated to each soul, some quickly, some delayed, some at the head and some at the foot. T103 brackets the corpus by restating the foundation: two substances from the beginning — light and darkness, the beautiful and the bitter, life and death — separating the beautiful forth from the darkness; regeneration is nothing other than the sorting of these two. T104's closing fragment names the Yes and the Amen as the Calling and the Hearing — the soul's answering that aids regeneration, helpers of the Divine Human in his ascent, refiners and remembrancers of the Living Soul, granting her remembrance whether in soul or tree or fashioned flesh.
